Vinegar is acetic acid in water, produced by Acetobacter oxidising the
alcohol in a previous ferment. The acetic acid content is what the
label means by percent acidity.

Acetic acid is the anomaly of the preserving acids: it is volatile,
which is to say you can smell it, and it that also means it is the
only acid that escapes a closed jar gradually. Lactic acid does not
evaporate. This is why a lacto-ferment keeps its sourness in storage
while a vinegar pickle loses strength over years.

Acetobacter wants oxygen and alcohol. A fermentation vessel that says
"vinegar" at the end usually started as a sealed ferment left open to
air — infection with intent.
